Focaccia forgives almost everything except a timid hand with the oil. Pour more than you think. Then pour a little more.

The dough is loose and shaggy at first. Leave it covered for half an hour and it relaxes into something you can stretch. Four sets of folds over two hours build the strength. You will feel it tighten under your palms.

Tip it into the oiled tin and push it to the corners. If it springs back, walk away for ten minutes. It will give in.

Dimple it hard, right to the bottom of the tin. Scatter rosemary and flaky salt. The kitchen fills with the green, resin smell of the rosemary as soon as it touches the oil.

Bake at 230 degrees until the top is deep gold and the edges fry in the oil. Lift it out of the tin at once, or the base steams and softens.

Before the oven door shuts, check that the oil has pooled in the dimples. Dry dimples bake into hard, bald patches.
